correctness.rationale: Finite target precisely M12. Direct exact mod-two chain check builds all 12,48,76,48,12 faces, boundary ranks 11,37,36,12; the 3 indicated induced octahedra give independent H2 generators and the rotation matrix with nilpotent ranks 2,1,0. Signed fixed-simplex enumeration yields integral-character Lefschetz traces 3,-1,-1,-1; cited published wedge-of-three-spheres theorem gives free integral degree-two homology of rank three and degree concentration. The character and finite order force rational eigenvalues -1,i,-i and rho^4=1 integrally. A saturated Z[i] plane, free sign quotient and lift calculation classify the extension by \(\mathbb Z[i]/(1+i)\cong\mathbb Z/2\); mod-two (rho-I)^2 nonzero proves the nonzero class and the displayed integer matrix. Direct Smith computation yields \(\mathbb Z/4\) coinvariants. No infinite extrapolation or omitted computational dependencies.

originality.rationale: The original Möbius-ladder homotopy theorem proves only the nonequivariant three-sphere wedge. The closest published full-result text gives the rational dihedral character, explicitly excluding integral lattices. The new claim distinguishes two integral lattices with identical rational modules by computing a length-three mod-two rotation Jordan block, deriving the sole nonzero Ext class, an explicit integral rotation matrix and Z/4 coinvariants. Search of aliases and related scientific claims did not disclose coverage. Residual unindexed priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The twelve-vertex Möbius ladder is the first nondegenerate positive-dimensional case with a three-dimensional independence-homology space, hence its integral rotation module is a natural previously undetermined object. Rational characters cannot distinguish its possible split and nonsplit cyclic order-four lattices. The exact nonsplit order-two extension and explicit \(\mathbb Z/4\) coinvariant group give structural arithmetic information and a concrete baseline for integral-equivariant investigations of the periodic family; they are not a textbook rephrasing of the known Betti number. The finite computation resolves this full natural rank-three lattice invariant.
